input: Set up a standing desk in the home office

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether 'set up' means assembling a new desk from scratch, converting an existing desk, or also includes arranging monitors, cables, and accessories — this determines how many steps and sub-tasks the plan needs.
Budget determines whether the user buys a premium electric height-adjustable desk, a mid-range hand-crank model, or a simple desktop converter — completely different plans.
Knowing if the user is doing this alone or with help affects task sequencing and whether steps like 'find an assistant for assembly' need to be included.
Whether a desk has already been purchased or still needs to be chosen and ordered changes the first actions entirely — research vs. assembly.
The available space and existing furniture arrangement determines whether the plan needs a room-clearing or cable-management phase before assembly begins.
Electric, manual crank, or desktop riser are fundamentally different products with different assembly complexity, cost, and ergonomic outcomes.
Whether 'done well' means just a functional desk or a fully ergonomic workstation (monitor arm, anti-fatigue mat, keyboard tray) defines the scope of the final checklist.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a standing desk in the home office
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to set up a standing desk in their home office, which could involve purchasing, assembling, and arranging the desk along with any accessories or ergonomic setup.

questions.title: Have you already bought the desk, or is that still ahead?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan starts with research and purchasing or jumps straight to assembly and setup.

questions.title: What type of standing desk do you want — electric, manual crank, or desktop riser?
questions.description: The desk type drives assembly complexity, cost, and the ergonomic outcome of the final setup.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: Budget narrows down which desk models and accessories are realistic options for the plan.

questions.title: Does 'set up' include monitors, cables, and accessories, or just the desk itself?
questions.description: Defines the full scope — whether the plan ends at assembly or extends to a complete ergonomic workstation.

questions.title: What does your target workspace look like right now — clear or cluttered?
questions.description: The current state of the room determines if clearing, measuring, or furniture-moving steps need to come first.

questions.title: Will you be assembling and moving the desk alone or with someone helping?
questions.description: Affects task sequencing and whether coordinating a helper needs to be an explicit step in the plan.

questions.title: What does a fully successful setup look like to you when it is done?
questions.description: Clarifies the finish line — a basic functional desk vs. a fully optimised ergonomic station with mat, monitor arm, and proper cable management.
